properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 9 at 4:13PM MST until September 9 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
SVRTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Santa Cruz County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 500 PM MST.

* At 413 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located near Patagonia,
moving southwest at 5 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Patagonia and Sonoita.

This includes Route 82 between mile markers 18 and 31.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Tucson.

homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

building.

killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to
be struck by lightning.

properties.description:

Lake Okeechobee...

At 655 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was located
over Liberty Point, moving west at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots and locally higher
waves. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm
passes.

water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded metal
objects.

Waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on the alert in
case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 9 at 3:14PM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot late-season conditions expected with high
temperatures up to 112 to 116 in Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 105 to 110 in the Las Vegas Valley, Moapa
Valley, and Pahrump Valley.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ to 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM CDT /NOON MDT/ TO 9 PM CDT /8
PM MDT/ THURSDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR AREAS
SOUTH AND WEST OF THE MISSOURI RIVER IN WESTERN AND SOUTH CENTRAL
NORTH DAKOTA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over western North Dakota
Thursday, ahead of an approaching cold front. Temperatures are
forecast to climb into the upper 80s, with afternoon humidities of 10
to 25 percent. Winds on Thursday afternoon are forecast to be
westerly 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 35 mph. Due to the low humidity
and breezy conditions with abundant dry vegetation, critical fire
weather conditions are expected Thursday afternoon into early
Thursday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of northwest, south central, and southwest
North Dakota.

* TIMING...From 1 PM CDT /noon MDT/ to 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ Thursday.

* WINDS...West winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 10 to 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

creeks.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 9 at 5:01PM EDT until September 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* RIP CURRENT IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely
for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the
beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* RIP CURRENT DETAILS...The rip current risk will be low this
morning at the ocean beaches, but increasing to moderate
through the afternoon and then high by late in the day as
southerly winds and surf increase.

* BEACH IMPACTS...Minor beach flooding is possible during the
times of high tide this evening through Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 9 at 12:22PM MST until September 11 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
107 to 110 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...The Yuma area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Riverton has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from noon to 9 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In Central WY Fire Zone....288.
In North Central WY Fire Zone....287.
In Northwest WY Fire Zone....286.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central WY...Fremont.
In North Central WY...Hot Springs...Park.
In West Central WY...Sublette.

* IMPACTS: Low Humidities and Strong Gusty Winds could cause
erratic fire behavior.

* WIND: West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 to 35 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 12 to 15 percent, especially at elevations
below 10,000 feet. RH recovery will be poor at elevations below
9,000 feet.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 108.

* WHERE...Portions of North and Central Texas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

tidal waterways (7.2 to 7.4 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston).

Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore
into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:31 PM today
at Charleston. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

impact information.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 9 at 3:14AM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above
normal during the day, with overnight lows also running 10 to 20
degrees above normal.

* WHERE...Bay Area and Central Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and in
heat-sensitive industries. Hot conditions can cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:48PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Hydrologic Concerns:
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with strong
south to southwesterly winds, could cause bankfull conditions or
minor flooding along the Kuskokwim and Johnson Rivers during high
tide.

Locations:
* Along Kuskokwim River, from Bethel south to Napakiak.
* Along Johnson River, from Nunapitchuk and Kasigluk south to the
Kuskokwim River.

Timing:
* Highest water levels will likely occur around high tide on Friday,
from about 11 AM through 4 PM.
* Strongest winds (south to southwesterly, gusting up to 30 to 45
mph) from about 4 PM Thursday through 4 PM Friday.

Next Steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED WATER LEVELS ALONG KUSKOKWIM AND JOHNSON RIVERS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:41PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with storm
surge flowing up river, could cause bankfull conditions or minor
flooding during high tide.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 4 PM.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Strong onshore winds could bring the potential for coastal erosion
and minor coastal flooding.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north, like
Toksook Bay and Tununak, may see higher water levels during
Thursday's high tide as well.

Next steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.
